alignments.note: The imperative takes the whole phrasal verb *Follow after*; no Greek preposition governs the object, so rule 36 does not remove *after* from the verb. Head on the lexical verb word.
Fronted accusative object rendered by the postposed *peace*; discontinuity permitted by rule 15.
Anarthrous substantival adjective with the supplied generic noun *men* as a rule 7 helper; rule 17's generic-noun clause heads on the adjective, as rule 51's anarthrous clause has it.
Article surfaces as English *the* under rule 19.
Noun to *sanctification*; the determiner stands on the article under rule 19, leaving the noun bare.
Improper preposition rendered by the single word *without*; rule 71's closing clause makes that word the head and no frame question arises. The governed relative is a separate unit under rule 2.
Relative pronoun to *which*; the English reorders preposition and relative, which rule 15 permits without merging the two units.

Negative indefinite carrying the clause's whole negation, with *man* the supplied generic completion; rule 17's generic-noun clause and rule 69's head on *any* both put the head on the negative word. No second negator stands, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Future indicative with its auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Article surfaces as English *the* under rule 19.
Noun to *Lord*, the determiner staying with its own article under rule 19.

review_notes: All 13 source and 17 target ids partitioned exactly once; every unit is aligned, with no unrepresented or added units in this verse.
s002 keeps *after* with the verb: the competing reading would give it to a preposition, but no Greek preposition governs Ἑιρήνην, so rule 36's warning about phrasal verbs does not apply.
s009/s008 are split rather than merged: rule 94's precondition for a compound prepositional unit is a single English word, and the ASV writes *without which* as two words each answering to a token.
